Plaintiffs' case in short was that the suit land i.e. 1/3rd of C.S. plot No. 839. 832. 842, 867 and 869 and half of C.S. plot No. 797 and whole of other plots appertaining to jama of Rs. 7/- belonged to Ichhamoyee Dashi who sold the same to Abdul Mannan an and pro forma defendant No.6 by kabala dated 28-2-36 in equal shares. Abdul Mannan sold his entire interest i.e. -/8/- annas share of the jama to the plaintiff by kabala dated 7-9-57 pro forma defendant No. 6 Jabed Mondal also sold some portion of the share of the jama to the plaintiff. The plaintiff and pro forma defendant No. 6 were threatened with dispossession and as such they filed Title Suit No. 205 of 1958 The suit ended in compromise by the said compromise decree. The plaintiff and pro forma defendant No.6 got 1/3rd share of the suit dag i.e. the suit land. The defendants 1 to 5 who were pro forma defendants Nos.30 to 34 in that suit got the remaining portion of the suit plot. Thereafter pro forma defendant No.6 sold his remaining share in the plot to the plaintiff and the plaintiff became owner of 16 annas share of the suit land and since then he was in possession of the same asserting his own right. In the recent rent roll plaintiffs name was not correctly recorded and being encouraged by the finding of a case under section 19(1) and 19(2) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the defendants threatened the plaintiff with dispossession from the suit land. Hence the suit. 

 9. Mr. M.H. Khondker appearing for the defendants appellants contended that Ext.2 did not divide the whole dags and even if it had purported to be done it was inadmissible in evidence not being registered as it compromised property outside suit inasmuch as such solenama is compulsorily registerable under section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act. The entire document has been placed before us and on reading of the Solenama we are of the view that the High Court Division in Letters Patent had correctly interoperated the document and rightly restored those of the trial and the lower appellate Court below. The expression ‘নালিশী জমি’ created the confusion but reading the solenama as a whole there is no doubt that the entire dags of the parties were divided as per the terms of the compromise. The interpretation of the Ext.2 is concluded by the concurrent findings of the facts of the courts below and the learned Single Judge in Second Appeal ought not to have disturbed those findings only on the assuming meaning of expression namely ‘নালিশী জমি’ which has now paved the way for controversy. The contention grounded on the admissibility of the document has no force. Section 17, no doubt, postulates that certain document must be registered but sub-section (2) provides that nothing in clause (b) and (c) of sub-section (1) applies to any decree or order of a court (except a decree or order ex pressed to be made on a compromise and comprising immovable property other than that which is the subject matter of the suit or proceeding). Clause 6 was amended in 1929 following a decision of Privy Council in Hemendra Kumari V. Midnapur Zamindary, A.I.R. 1919 P.C. 79. After the amendment the position appears to be this: If the case of compromise relates to property which is not the subject matter of the suit or proceeding then obviously latter part of Clause 6 would take away the exception and to such a case clause (b) or (c) as the case may be would apply and such a document would be liable for registration. Where the compromise deals only with the properties in suit and the Court passes a decree in accordance therewith such a case will fall within the exception and such a decree would not require registration. The words "and not being decree and order: in section 50 obviously refer to decrees and orders which are exempted from registration under the amended section 17(2) (vi). It is a question of fact whether the compromise has been acted upon or is covered by a decree which is a mixed question. If the compromise has been acted upon or is covered by decree then it is settled law that compromise is exempt from registration.
